title: Published package entrypoint requires a dev-only dependency
reasoning: The package is publishable (`private: false`) and declares `src/main/index.cjs` as its Node entrypoint, but that entrypoint immediately requires `electron`. Electron is only listed in devDependencies, not dependencies or peerDependencies, so an npm consumer installing `windieos` and importing/requiring the package without this repo's dev dependencies will fail at module resolution before any API can be used.
reproduction: From a clean consumer project, install the packed/published frontend package with production dependencies only, then run `node -e "require('windieos')"`; Node will attempt to load `src/main/index.cjs` and fail to resolve `electron`.
recommendation: Either make this package non-publishable/private, expose a real library-safe entrypoint that does not require Electron at import time, or declare Electron as an explicit runtime/peer dependency and document that the package is an Electron app entrypoint rather than a general Node library.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for npm packing, production install shape, or requiring the published package entrypoint from a clean consumer project.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a packaging smoke test that runs `npm pack`, installs the tarball into a temporary project with production dependencies, and verifies the declared `main` can be resolved or intentionally fails with a documented package type.
minimumFixScope: frontend/package.json plus any new dedicated package entrypoint needed to separate publishable library API from Electron app bootstrap.
